Hello everyone, and welcome to FH6 Redux. This is a project that I'm delighted to share for free with the community, however, if you feel you want to support me, there is a link in the spreadsheet to do so, thank you\!

**What is FH6 Redux?**  
FH6 Redux is a reimagining of the single-player experience in Forza Horizon 6, designed to make progression feel more meaningful, immersive and rewarding. Whilst FH6 is a phenomenal racing game, I wanted to create a career experience inspired by classic progression-focused racing games of the past such as Forza Motorsport 1, Gran Turismo 4, NFS Most Wanted ‘05 and Test Drive Unlimited; one where every car purchase matters, every championship feels earned and every journey across the map has purpose.

**Requirements:**  
✓ Obtained a Gold Wristband.  
✓ Obtained a Yellow Stamp in Discover Japan  
✓ Completed every Road, Dirt and CC event in the game.  
✓ Discovered every Street and Touge event in the game.  
✓ A fair amount of in-game credits (100k+ is a comfortable starting point).  
✓ A 1992 Nissan Skyline GT-R with cool cosmetics and a striking paint job, upgraded to the top of S1 Class (you don't get to keep it).  
✓ A stock 2017 Toyota JPN Taxi (you don't get to keep it).

**Optional:**  
An empty in-game garage after you purchase your first car.  
No photos taken of any cars/landmarks.  
No barn finds or treasure cars discovered.  
No stories completed.

**Preface:**  
You've already conquered Japan in-game. What Redux asks you to do is experience it again, as if for the first time. The cars in your garage, the credits in your account, and the events you've completed; mentally, those belong to a different driver. Redux is your second story.

This spreadsheet requires two things: First, access to a computer (you can use it on a phone but certain things aren't usable) and the patience to track everything; and second, being comfortable with separating what happens in-game from what happens in the spreadsheet. In-game you may earn 10,000Cr for completing a race, whereas in Redux it may only be 2,500Cr, in-game you may have hundreds of cars, in Redux you may only have 2, etc. If this is not for you, it's not for you and nothing will change that. But if you can accept those two things, then let's continue.

**To Begin:**  
**Make a copy of the spreadsheet by going to ‘File' and then ‘Make a copy'. Then allow access to the following message: “Warning: Some formulas are trying to send and receive data from external parties”. This will allow you to Roll Championships and Used Cars.**

_Ensure you have a 1992 Nissan Skyline GT-R with cool cosmetics and a striking paintjob, upgraded to the top of S1 Class. Also ensure you have a stock 2017 Toyota JPN Taxi. Drive the GT-R to the exit of Ito Airfield, ideally around sunset._

_You start on a plane, heading to Tokyo._

_You look out your window to see the city and the beautiful hills and mountains in the distance, including Mount Fuji. You also spot, beautifully lit by the setting sun, the Horizon Festival: The annual World's Greatest Amateur Racing Competition and simultaneously World's Biggest Celebration of Cars and Music. It's in Japan this year, and is days away from starting, though it may as well have already started, as you and thousands of others have descended upon the country to compete and enjoy the festivities._

_After landing, you exit the airport. You spot Mei, a longtime friend who has come to pick you up. She's a Tokyo local and like you, is mad into cars._

**Mei**  
“Hey\!”  
(You both embrace each other with a hug)  
**Mei (cont.)**  
“How was the flight?”  
**You**  
“Oh not too bad, I had a lovely view of the city when we were landi-”

_You spot Mei's heavily modified 1992 Nissan Skyline GT-R._

**You (cont.)**  
“Is that…? Wow\!”  
**Mei**  
“Oh my god I totally forgot you've never seen my Skyline\! She's a dream, isn't she?”  
**Mei (cont.)**  
“Hey, do you wanna drive it?”  
**You**  
“Really?”  
**Mei**  
“Yeah, back to the house.”  
**You**  
“Alright\!”  
**Mei**  
“Just don't scratch it\!”

_You both get into the car._

_Drive Mei's 1992 Nissan Skyline GT-R from Ito Airfield exit to Mei's House. I recommend sticking to traffic laws, whilst occasionally opening up the car on open stretches._

_As you drive you spot advertising for the Horizon Festival everywhere._

**Mei**  
“So (insert your name), what's the plan?”  
**You**  
“I don't really know, well, first things first I need a car…”

**Mei**  
“You should be able to pick one up fairly quickly, there's dealerships all over the city and beyond. I'm working tomorrow so you'd have to get a taxi but when we're home we can look together on some websites.”  
**You**

_You arrive at Mei's House. Park outside and continue reading._

**Mei**  
“Here we are… oh and if you ever need help fixing up a car just drop by here and we can have a look together, I'm not as good as those gurus at the Festival but I am free\!”  
**You**  
“I'm sure you're just as good as they are”  
**Mei**  
“Eh, maybe one day…”

_Inside the house you settle in._

**Mei**  
“Hey, wanna use this?”

_Mei points to her computer._

**You**  
“Yeah sure, thanks.”

_You both sit down._

**Mei**  
“Okay here we are. Now you can probably afford something decent, but remember that if you want to enter one of the Festival Campaigns you need to pay the 30,000 Credit buy-in, so don't buy a car that leaves you with less than that if you want to enter.”

_At this point you must decide which car to purchase. Refer to ‘New Cars' to see the price of each and every car in the game, alternatively, perform a roll in ‘Used Cars' to see today's used cars. Your budget is 45,000Cr and entry to a Horizon Campaign is 30,000Cr, though you are not obliged to enter a Campaign straight away. Crucially, don't purchase the car once you've decided on it._

**Mei**  
“Nice choice\! I'll call a taxi in the morning, on me.”  
**You**  
“Thanks Mei, you've been a great help.”

_At the crack of dawn, get in a 2017 Toyota JPN Taxi and, obeying traffic laws, drive it to the location of your manufacturer's dealership (see dealership locations in the spreadsheet), or a random location on the map if buying a used car. Once you have arrived at your location, open the Autoshow or Auction House and buy your car, then fast travel back to the dealership's location to simulate you driving out of the dealership with it._

_At this point, you may now go back to the spreadsheet and take a look at the Activities in ‘Start Here', though I would read this guide to the end first._

_I liken this moment to RuneScape (if you have played it). After you complete Tutorial Island, you get teleported to Lumbridge. From that point, the game is fully open, you can do whatever you want, as long as you're eligible. This is the same here. If you want to focus on the Festival Campaigns you can, if you want to just do Street Races you can, if you want to endlessly free-roam you can. This is an open single-player experience and the path you take is totally up to you._

_However, if you would like some direction to begin, there is no better place to start than the ‘Road Racing' tab, as long as you've bought a D Class car and have the funds to pay the Buy-In. Alternatively, if you've bought a car that left you without the funds to enter either Campaign yet, maybe try out ‘Street Racing' or visit ‘Licence Tests' to earn a D Class Licence and begin ‘Club Racing'._

**Before you dive in, let me just do a bit of housekeeping, in no particular order:**  
_Explore the entire spreadsheet before doing anything, have a read of each and every tab as there is a lot to take in._

**\*11/06/2026 EDIT:** A lot of people are asking about drivers in the spreadsheet vs Drivatars in-game. You can either: 1\) Manually assign each spreadsheet driver to each Drivatar pre-race for each race (slower) or 2\) Randomly assign race results to each spreadsheet driver (faster).\*

_Every championship within the spreadsheet uses F1's points system, explained in Road and Offroad Racing tabs._

_To set up an event, you'll need to drive to the event's location, choose ‘Custom Race', and then decide any car restrictions that may apply, along with race conditions. Visit the ‘Climate' tab to be given a time of day and weather forecast for each event. I also recommend turning Rewind Off and Simulation Damage On for all events and picking a suitable AI Difficulty to challenge you._

_You need to decide which 11 drivers join you in any championship. If you're struggling to come up with some names, [this](https://www.behindthename.com/random/) is a great website for generating names. Be sure to give them nationalities and their appropriate flags from the ‘Flags' tab. Consider that a lot of racers in this year's Festival will be Japanese this year._

_Any custom-built races have no checkpoints. This, along with turning Rewind Off should increase the stakes of each race. Yes, if you really want to, you can cheat and drive straight to the finish, but where's the fun in that? Stick to the road, be fair when racing the AI and be sure to either have your mini-map or the full racing line turned On for any custom-made events so you know where you're going and don't take a wrong turn ten miles in. I also recommend turning the AI difficulty up by one for any custom-made events._

_I recommend playing Redux in Horizon Solo; the world feels more alive with Drivatars and you can challenge them to Impromptu Races. Here are the credits you will win or lose depending on their ability and outcome:_  
**\*Easy:** Win \= 250Cr Loss \= \-750Cr\*  
**\*Medium:** Win \= 500Cr Loss \= \-500Cr\*  
**\*Hard:** Win \= 750Cr Loss \= \-250Cr\*

_Ignore credits/cars received from playing online, levelling up, both journals, wheelspins, gifts, daily payouts or any other form. That said, many cars in the game are only obtainable via the Playlist, Wheelspins, etc, so feel free to keep these if you want in case you wish to purchase them in Redux later._

_Ignore ‘Change Car' and actually drive to the house where your car is to get into it. Also don't Fast Travel (unless you have to), it's a driving game after all\!_

_Whilst Redux is a single-player experience, there is nothing stopping you and your friends playing it together._
